chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurarah, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydillah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He was asked about the alms-tax (zakat). He said: 'The zakat is obligatory on nine things: on gold and silver, on wheat and barley, on dates and raisins, on camels, on cattle, and on sheep. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pardoned/exempted whatever is besides that.'
ai.seo_question: What are the nine specific items subject to zakat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the foundational nine categories of zakat, reflecting the classical Shia view that zakat is strictly limited to these specific assets rather than being a general tax on all wealth. The mention of 'camels, cattle, and sheep' as distinct categories highlights the agrarian economic context of the Prophet's time, while the phrase 'exempted whatever is besides these' underscores the principle of *al-aw'liya* (primacy of the text) in limiting obligatory dues. This narration serves as a primary evidence for Shia jurists when debating the extension of zakat to modern currencies and goods through *qiyas* (analogy) or *ijtihad*.
